body:
Hi,

I could not reproduce this with a simple hello world application and using a cURL request:

`curl -H "X-Forwarded-For: 10.17.13.17" http://localhost:8080/hello`

Is there anything more you can tell us what you are doing?
I will take another look. But it looks like an NPE can be provoked somehow. I will try to reproduce and otherwise analyze the code.
The only way I saw that would cause a NPE is if the host is somehow null (I don't know how that can happen)

When I call an endpoint using `curl` like this I can provoke this NPE: `curl http://localhost:8080/foo -H "Host:"`. I can't really tell you how this happened now, but an NPE seems wrong in any case.

So in summary: When `quarkus.http.proxy.proxy-address-forwarding` is set to `true` and an empty `Host` header is provided, then an NPE is thrown.
That is good enough. I'll provide a fix, because certainly we don't want a NPE.

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
I got the following error and stack trace reported when a request was sent with the following header `X-Forwarded-For: 10.17.13.17`. I don't know for sure if this is the header which caused the problem, that is just my assumption. I am however quite sure this problem didn't exist before Quarkus 1.11.0.Final.


issue.body:
### Describe the bug

I see NPEs in the access logs when at least the Host-HTTP-Header is broken/invalid.

This looks like a regression of issue #14536.

### Expected behavior

No NPE and stacktrace in the logs.

### Actual behavior

_No response_

### How to Reproduce?

1. Create a quarkus starter project (with Gradle)
2. Enable JAX-RS
3. Create simple HelloWorld resource
4. Set quarkus.http.access-log.enabled=true
5. Run it
6. Execute `curl -H "Host:" http://localhost:8080/foo -Lv`

### Output of `uname -a` or `ver`

Linux redacted 6.5.0-14-generic #14-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Tue Nov 14 14:59:49 UTC 2023 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### Output of `java -version`

OpenJDK Runtime Environment (build 17.0.9+9-Ubuntu-123.10)

### Quarkus version or git rev

3.6.6

### Build tool (ie. output of `mvnw --version` or `gradlew --version`)

Gradle 8.5

### Additional information

I know that the real culprit is not the mentioned cURL-request . I see the exact kind of stack traces in the log, but don't know the definite source of it. I can narrow it down to a Nagios health check, but don't know the exact request and headers, yet. I'll try to provide that information when I got a real TCP dump of it.
